title: Poultry Safety
guidelines: Never wash raw poultry, as it splashes bacteria around the kitchen.
Use separate cutting boards and utensils for raw poultry.
Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after handling raw poultry.
Cook all poultry to a safe minimum internal temperature to destroy harmful bacteria.

title: Red Meat Safety
guidelines: Ground meats must be cooked to a higher temperature than whole cuts because surface bacteria is mixed throughout the meat during grinding.
Let whole cuts of meat rest for 3 minutes after cooking before carving to ensure safety and retain juices.

title: Seafood Safety
guidelines: Buy seafood only from reputable sources.
If serving fish raw (like sushi), it must be 'sushi-grade' and previously frozen according to FDA guidelines to kill parasites.
Cook fish until it is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.

critical_temperatures.shellfish: Cook until shells open; discard any that don't open.

title: Egg Safety
guidelines: Keep eggs refrigerated at 40°F (4°C) or below.
Cook eggs until both the yolk and white are firm, unless using pasteurized eggs.
For recipes requiring raw or lightly cooked eggs (like mayo or Caesar dressing), use pasteurized shell eggs or pasteurized egg products.

critical_temperatures.eggs: Cook until yolks and whites are firm.

title: Dairy Safety
guidelines: Store dairy products at 40°F (4°C) or below.
Discard dairy that has been left at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
Use pasteurized milk and cheeses, especially for pregnant women, young children, and immunocompromised individuals.

title: Pressure Cooking Safety
guidelines: Never fill the pressure cooker more than two-thirds full. For foods that expand (rice, beans), do not fill more than half full.
Always check that the steam release valve and vent are clean and unobstructed before use.
Never force a pressure cooker open. Wait until all pressure has released naturally or via the quick release valve.
Keep hands and face away from the steam release valve when venting.

title: Deep Frying Safety
guidelines: Never overfill the pot with oil; keep it less than half full to account for bubbling up when food is added.
Ensure food is completely dry before adding to hot oil to prevent dangerous splattering.
Never leave heating oil unattended. If it smokes, turn off the heat immediately.
Keep a class K or B fire extinguisher, or a heavy metal lid nearby. Never use water on a grease fire.

title: Food Storage Safety
guidelines: Follow the 'Danger Zone' rule: do not leave perishable food between 40°F and 140°F (4°C - 60°C) for more than 2 hours.
Store raw meat on the bottom shelf of the refrigerator to prevent juices from dripping onto other foods.
Cool hot foods rapidly before refrigerating by dividing into smaller, shallow containers.

title: Reheating Safety
guidelines: Reheat all leftovers to 165°F (74°C) internal temperature.
Bring sauces, soups, and gravies to a rolling boil when reheating.
When microwaving, cover food and stir occasionally to eliminate cold spots where bacteria can survive.

title: Allergen Management
guidelines: Thoroughly clean and sanitize all surfaces, equipment, and hands after handling major allergens (nuts, shellfish, soy, dairy, etc.).
Be aware of hidden allergens in sauces, stocks, and condiments.
Always inform guests of potential cross-contamination if preparing allergen-free meals in a shared kitchen.

title: Cross-Contamination Prevention
guidelines: Use separate cutting boards (color-coded if possible) for raw meats and produce.
Never place cooked food back onto a plate that held raw meat without washing it first.
Wash hands for 20 seconds with warm water and soap after handling raw meats, taking out trash, or using the restroom.

title: Knife Handling Safety
guidelines: A sharp knife is safer than a dull knife because it requires less pressure to cut.
Always cut away from your body and keep your fingers tucked in a 'claw' shape holding the food.
Never try to catch a falling knife; step back and let it drop.
Place a damp paper towel under your cutting board to prevent it from slipping.
